description:
If you're looking for your first home and want somewhere you can quite comfortably move straight into without having a long list of jobs to do, then this could be a great option for you.

Situated on Limestone Close in Great Blakenham, this property has been owned by the current owners from new, and they've done a lovely job of looking after it. It's fresh, modern and well presented throughout, with some lovely additions, including decorative wall panelling, updated flooring and landscaping to both the front and rear of the property.

One of the things that sets this house apart from many similar properties is the addition of a really good-sized garage that comfortably fits a large car. Alongside the nicely paved frontage, driveway parking and EV charging point, you've got plenty of space for your parking needs.

Stepping through the front door, you've got a nice entrance hallway with a downstairs WC to your left and the kitchen and dining room to your right. It's a nicely proportioned kitchen, with plenty of worktop and cupboard space whilst still allowing enough room to comfortably sit down and enjoy dinner together.

To the rear of the property is the living room. Spanning the full width of the house, it's a lovely space to get comfortable on the sofa at the end of the day. The French doors allow plenty of natural light into the room and, throughout the summer months, it's nice to be able to open these up and make the most of the garden.

Upstairs, there are three bedrooms and the family bathroom. The two larger bedrooms are generous doubles, with the main bedroom also benefiting from built-in storage. The third bedroom, whilst slightly smaller, currently accommodates a double bed, although it would equally work well as a nursery or a home office, depending on your needs.

The rear garden is a really manageable size, with a patio area immediately outside the French doors and the remainder predominantly laid to lawn. There's enough space to enjoy having friends and family over in the summer or for the dog to run around, without having to dedicate your entire weekend to maintaining it.

Thanks to the positioning of the house within the development, it also enjoys a little more privacy than you might typically expect from a property of this nature.

You've got direct access into the garage from the garden, too. Whether you're using it to park the car, store your bikes and outdoor equipment or even create a little home gym, having that additional space is a real benefit.

Now, one of the things I particularly like about Great Blakenham is that you get to enjoy that slightly more rural feel without having to sacrifice the convenience of having everything you need nearby.

Within a couple of minutes of leaving the house, you can be on the A14, heading towards Ipswich, Stowmarket or Bury St Edmunds. Equally, you can leave the car at home and enjoy some lovely walks along the River Gipping, taking you in one direction towards Bramford Meadows and in the other towards Needham Market and its lake. It's a particularly lovely location if you've got a dog or simply enjoy getting outdoors.

Within walking distance of the property, you've got a Tesco Express, an Indian restaurant, a local gym, the village hall and recreation ground. The neighbouring village of Claydon offers even more, including a Co-op, a couple of lovely local pubs in the Greyhound and the Crown, as well as local schools.

For those who need to commute by train, you've also got the benefit of railway stations at both Needham Market, Ipswich and Stowmarket within driving distance.

The development itself is now nicely established and, unlike some modern developments, doesn't feel overly crowded, with a good provision of parking throughout.

For me, it's the combination of the condition of the house, the additional space provided by the garage and the convenience of the location that makes this such an appealing first home. Somewhere you can get the keys, get your furniture in and simply start enjoying living there.

description:
Situated to the East of Ipswich is this fully refurbished, two bedroom mid terrace home benefitting from off road parking and a south facing garden.

Description - This stylishly presented two-bedroom mid-terrace has been comprehensively refurbished to a high modern standard, combining contemporary finishes with practical living space in the popular east Ipswich location.  A welcoming entrance leads into the dining room featuring bespoke fitted sideboard units and access through to the sitting room which is fitted with a contemporary media wall with large wall-mounted television and a modern fireplace. The fully fitted modern kitchen has soft-grey shaker-style units with warm wooden worktops and fitted appliances. Upstairs there are two double bedrooms both with fitted wardrobes and a Contemporary family bathroom.  Herringbone flooring with under floor heating has been fitted to the whole of the ground floor whilst modern radiators are upstairs, there is double glazing, oak doors and sensored lighting on the landing.

Location - The property is situated to the east of Ipswich and is within walking distances of local shops and also within easy reach of Rose Hill Primary and Copleston High School. The town centre is also within easy reach with its shopping and recreational facilities as well as its rejuvenated water front with bars restaurants and marina. Ipswich main line railway station offers a fast and frequent rail service to London's Liverpool street, journey scheduled just over the hour.

Entrance Porch - Double glazed window to front, oak door to accommodation.

Dining Room - 3.53m x 3.18m (11'07 x 10'05) - Double glazed window to front,  herringbone floor with under floor heating and bespoke cupboard either side of chimney.

Sitting Room - 3.48m x 3.28m (11'05 x 10'09) - Double glazed window to rear, media wall with tv to remain and electric flame effect fire, and herringbone floor with under floor heating.

Kitchen - 4.70m x 1.88m (15'05 x 6'02) - Double glazed window and door to side, grey shaker style kitchen with oak worktops above, composite sink, integrated oven and microwave, integrated induction hob, integrated dishwasher, plumbing for washing machine, space for freestanding fridge/freezer and herringbone floor with under floor heating.

First Floor Landing - Oak doors to bedrooms, sensor lighting, access to the boarded loft via a large hatch with pull down ladder and carpet flooring.

Bedroom One - 3.48m x 3.20m (11'05 x 10'06) - Double glazed window to front, wardrobes either side of the chimney to remain, tall anthracite radiator and carpet flooring.

Bedroom Two - 3.28m x 2.51m (10'09 x 8'03) - Double glazed window to rear, tall anthracite radiator, fitted cupboard and carpet flooring.

Bathroom - 2.54m x 1.96m (8'04 x 6'05) - Double glazed window to rear, large freestanding bath, vanity unit with sink, shower cubicle, low level wc, heated towel rail, polished porcelain wall and floor tiles.

Outside And Gardens - To the of the property there is a driveway which has been recently laid and provides off road parking for one vehicle. A side gate leads to the rear south facing garden which benefits from a patio area, a raised astro turf lawn and a shed with power and lighting.

Services - We understand the property is connected to mains electric, gas, water and drainage.
